project.name: Maestro Style Reel — How Chinese Characters Began as Pictures

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Every Chinese character began as a picture. Not a code, not an alphabet. A drawing of something a person could actually see.
entries.direction: Warm, unhurried, opening a story. Slight smile.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Start with a mountain. Three peaks, the middle one tallest. Anyone can draw that, and three thousand years ago, someone did.
entries.direction: Conversational, as if sketching while speaking.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Then hands copied it. Thousands of hands, over thousands of years. A brush is faster than a picture, so the curves pulled straight.
entries.direction: Reflective, letting the long span of time land.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: And there it is. Mountain. The three peaks never left.
entries.direction: Quiet satisfaction, like showing someone the answer.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Water was drawn as a current running downward, with droplets thrown off to either side.
entries.direction: Descriptive, tracing the shape with the voice.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Straighten the current. Keep the droplets. That is the character for water.
entries.direction: Two crisp beats, then a settled reveal.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: The sun was easy. A circle. But a circle on its own means very little, so a mark went in the middle to say: this one is the sun.
entries.direction: Light, a little amused at the practicality of it.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Squares are quicker to write than circles. So the sun became this. It is also the word for day.
entries.direction: Matter of fact, with a small lift on the last sentence.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: The moon got a crescent, precisely because the sun had already taken the round shape. It is also the word for month.
entries.direction: Gentle, letting the logic click into place.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Now the interesting part. Once you have pictures, you can put them together.
entries.direction: Leaning in. A turn in the story.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: A person, seen from the side. Two legs, caught mid stride.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Set one person behind another, and the meaning follows straight from the picture. To follow.
entries.direction: Pleased, as if handing over a small gift.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: A tree. Two trees make a grove. Three trees make a forest, and the character is exactly that.
entries.direction: Building in three clear steps, faster each time.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: This is why looking closely at Chinese pays off. The characters are not arbitrary marks to memorize. They are drawings, stacked and simplified, still carrying the picture they started as.
entries.direction: Warm close, slowing into the final line.
